brief: The canvas displays an abstract, three-dimensional representation of an origami crane constantly undergoing transformation. Initially, the viewer sees the crane constructed from several interlocking, brightly colored planes of paper. These planes do not remain static; instead, they writhe and shift, executing a perpetual cycle of folding and unfolding. The structure repeatedly blossoms fully into a graceful crane shape, only to instantly begin collapsing back into its constituent folded layers, restarting the mesmerizing metamorphosis over and over again. The entire piece is a continuous loop of architectural movement, generating visual complexity solely through its own self-contained motion.
prompt: an origami crane folding and unfolding itself forever
statement: This sketch depicts an abstract, three-dimensional origami crane in perpetual motion. The crane is composed of multiple interlocking planes that continuously fold and unfold in a mesmerizing cycle. Using the WEBGL renderer, I created a series of rotating geometric planes that transform their positions and orientations over time, simulating the natural flow of paper folding and unfolding. The animation is self-contained and driven entirely by mathematical functions, creating an endless metamorphosis of form. The planes shift through various configurations, transitioning from a structured crane shape back into its constituent folded layers, generating visual complexity through pure motion rather than static geometry.
